topic.name: Uh Oh, Canada
topic.description: Articles related to Uh Oh, Canada

content_html_sanitized:
And how did the elite crowd react to his courage in taking on this controversial issue? According to the Canadian Press, with applause - and a few whoops of joy. Ah, such courage!

Of course, this has been the worst kept secret in Canada. Justice Minister Martin Cauchon, who is supposedly in favor of legalization, has been saying that he wants to decriminalize for almost a year, and now says that the bill will be introduced in June
See
 Canadian Justice Minister Cites UK Move In Trial Balloon on " Decriminalization. " Police Want to Keep " Hammer. " Reporting from Haarlem in The Netherlands.

He could not even have hinted at this, if he had not had Chretien's approval, but many observers still thought that it might yet be allowed to die. Now it seems certain, but it is not at all certain to me that this is going to be a good thing.

From 2001 see
 Leader of Canadian Tories Supports " Decriminalization " Not " Legalization " -- Again. This Makes Mere " Decriminalization " a Defeat for Us. Defining Our Terms and Setting Our Goals.

As always, the devil is in the details, and Chretien has only said that it will be like a traffic ticket. " So you will have another ticket, for losing your senses, or something like that. " Isn't that cute!

But he added, " At the same time, we will have a drug strategy to discourage young people from using drugs and which will target drug traffickers. "

Does this mean a nationwide campaign of reefer madness and stiffer penalties for growers?
See
 Canada Exports A Little Reefer to DEAland. Imports A Lot of Reefer Madness. A Bad Balance of Trade. Canadian Taxpayers Are Being Lied to At Their Own Expense, But It May Also Cost Them Their Freedom.
and
 Canadian Justice Minister Calls for National Debate On Cannabis Policies And Begins It By Debating Himself. Phony Decrim Bill May Be Used As Cover To Increase Penalties for Growing.

My good friend John Conroy, QC, will be heading to Ottawa Saturday to argue the challenge to the possession laws before the Supreme Court next Tuesday.
See
 Canadian Supreme Court Punts On Cannabis Cases Until Spring. The Games Governments Play Prove The Need for International Debate on Cannabis Prohibition. Special to MarijuanaNews
and
 Ontario Judge Prods Canadian Government On Medical Cannabis Program. Supreme Court Hearings On All Cannabis Prohibition Now Set For May. We Are Winning!

He has eloquently expressed his concerns, which follow.
From John Conroy:

The Government move to traffic tickets-- for simple possession only-- may result in further court challenges, time, energy and costs, and will prove much more difficult to undo. I think it will take even longer to undo, and may well fail in the courts because there will no longer be a threat to physical liberty. It will be interesting to see what happens for non-payment of the fines. It is now usual to order distress against the persons goods i.e. seizing and selling them. I don't know how often this happens in practice. It used to be that you went to prison in default of payment resulting in more poor people in prisons.

Growing (producing), trafficking (including 'giving'), possession for the purpose of trafficking and even possession over the prescribed limit of perhaps as low as 10 grams (although Cauchon supposedly wants it be to be 30 grams) will remain in the Controlled Drugs and Substance Act and their argument is that they will concentrate on this element and maybe even try to justify heavier penalties. This is exactly what the USA wants. Like some 13 states that have had traffic ticket schemes for possession since the sixties, Canada will simply become one of them but the main war will continue or even escalate. Will they turn a blind eye to coffee shops and cannabis contests?

I think this is a deliberately timed announcement designed to undercut to some extent our arguments, at least in Caine, (the personal possession case) and to perhaps put off or forestall these efforts over the last ten years of trying to get this case before the highest court and get a decision from them on this point that would preclude even any such traffic ticket scheme.

While this kind of incrementalism may have been acceptable 20 years ago, surely it is simply not acceptable today, given the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms and the state of our constitutional rights to liberty and the security of our persons and the right not to have them taken away or even threatened except in accordance with the " principles of fundamental justice ".

If your conduct does not pose a 'significant' risk of harm to another or others or society as a whole then it should not result in your physical liberty being threatened by the use of the criminal law.

If your conduct does not pose any risk of harm to another or others or society as a whole then why should you be at risk of being stopped or in any way interfered with by the state. From what source does the State derive its interest and right to control you in that way? The government scheme is an attack on cannabis culture. It says you continue to deserve to be stigmatized for your use. It says you are not worthy of being treated equally before and under the law and are not deserving of the equal
protection and equal benefit of the law without discrimination because of your intoxicant of choice, not because of any impact on them.

It may appear to be a move in the right direction but I have grave doubts that it will be in fact. I hope I'm wrong. I hope I can get a decent legal non political decision out of the court and then - time will again tell.

Conroy is right in assuming that the DEAland narks really won't have any problems with this, although they will make a few threatening noises.

In fact, a Quebec paper, LeDevoir, reports that DEAland Ambassador to Canada, Paul Cellucci, believes that the reform could actually make the law tougher.

Cellucci says, " For the moment, if a person is picked up in possession of marijuana, he goes before the court and nothing happens: no fine, no threat of a prison sentence, nothing! But, if a person must pay a fine of $500, perhaps that will make it less available. "

Oddly, the very prohibitionist Toronto Chief of Police, Julian Fantino, seems to agree with Conroy, but for other reasons. Fantino says, " If the government wants to blink and wink and turn its backs on organized crime and endanger the lives of ... law-abiding citizens, then they should just legalize it and get it over with and the police will be done with it. "
See
 Toronto Police Chief Supports Decrim -- At the Option of The Narks And " Education Or Treatment Programs " For Marijuana Users. The Therapeutic Police State. -- 2 Articles

Obviously, I don't think that Fantino has become a legalizer, but he is right about the problems with leaving the supply in the black market.

A Reuters story by David Ljunggren even follows the party line, telling Americans,U.S. police say Canada, with an estimated illegal drug market of C$14 billion ($9.7 billion), has surpassed Mexico as a source of illegal drugs for the United States.

Of course, that is an absurd lie, but where would the US police get such an idea? From the head of the Canadian Police Association.
See
 As Canada Moves Toward Some Form Of Decriminalization, Canadian Narks and Walters Escalate Lying. The New Math. Canada Replaces Mexico As Leading Supplier of Cannabis. And If You Believe That

For the official Canadian data on cultivation see http://www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/crimint/cultivation_e.htm

However, Jason Botchford, whose articles have been running in the Sun tabloids all week, has been doing his homework. He actually reports the data.

Where Canada Ranks According To A United Nations Report On The Amount Of Cannabis Seized In 2000. Amounts Are In Kilograms:
Country - Amount - % of world seizures
1. Mexico - 2,050,402 - 46%
2. South Africa - 717,702 - 16%
3. Malawi - 312,472 - 6%
4. United States - 218,256 - 5%
5. Brazil - 159,073 - 4%
6. India - 100,056 - 2%
7. Colombia - 75,465 - 2%
8. Canada - 70,222 - 2%
9. Jamaica - 55,859 - 1.5%
10. Paraguay - 51,081 - 1.5%
Source: United Nations Office On Drugs And Crime * Global Illicit Drug Trends
See
 How Marijuana Prohibition Really Works on the Texas/Mexico Border. Contrast with the Situation at the Canadian Border. Great Journalism.
and
 Now, How the Narks Created Smack in Mexico. Replacing Marijuana With Poppies. The Iron Law of Prohibition Keeps Working, But The Media Don't

Botchford also quotes a DEAland nark:

" Canada is not talking about legalizing large indoor grows or stopping the arrests of criminal enterprises, " said Drug Enforcement Agency ( DEA ) spokesman Will Glaspy. " Essentially that's where the ( border ) problems are. People wanting to smoke dope and get high is not a cross-border issue.

" But it ( a decriminalization policy ) is going to increase our security along the border because marijuana is a Schedule 1 illicit drug. If Canada changed its laws, it's not going to change things here in the U.S. and you'd have a lot of people wanting to get high who would be going to a border to have a look. "

Or they could just go to Ohio where 100 grams gets a $100 fine.

In any case, there is still the problem that nothing is being done about complying with the Ontario court order that requires the Canada come up with a workable medical cannabis program, or there is no law against possession in Ontario, the largest province.

In January, Judge Sidney Lederman of Ontario's Superior Court declared the Marijuana Medicinal Access Regulations unconstitutional. He gave Health Canada until July 9th to fix the regulations or supply the medical cannabis itself. Health Canada has appealed the decision, but the deadline remains.

A representative of Health Canada said, " We are working toward having the appeal heard, with the hope that the deadline would change. But if Ottawa loses the appeal or cannot change the deadline, " we will be caught, and so we are looking at all our options. "
See
 Canada Discovers The Netherlands As Senator Nolin Goes To Washington. What Bush/Ashcroft/Walters Really Fear: An Honest Debate On The Issues. We Are Winning!

Ann McClellan, the incompetent Health Minister, is in hot water over her mishandling of the Toronto SARS scare, but her mishandling of the medical cannabis program is even more scandalous.
See
 Canadian Health Minister Seeks Asylum In DEAland; Says Making Her Think About Medical Cannabis Constitutes Torture. In DC They Don't Allow That Sort of Thing. Thinking, That Is.

This could undermine the government's effort just to decriminalize, and leave Canada with no law on possession, even before the Supreme Court rules around the end of the year.

Meanwhile, The Toronto Star reports, Decriminalizing possession of small amounts of pot for personal use has the support of the man most likely to be the next prime minister of Canada. (Paul Martin)

" I think the idea of giving a young person a criminal record because they happened to get caught with a very, very small quantity ( five to 30 grams ) once in their life -- I don't think that's what we should be doing, " Liberal leadership candidate Paul Martin told Sun Media.

But Martin added: " I would not, under any circumstances, make it legal. "

Now consider that last statement. What if Martin really means that?

It should worry all Canadians, not just supporters of legalization. Taken at face value, it would mean that the suppression of cannabis is the highest priority of the Canadian government, just as it is in DEAland, which is why I call The United States of America, my country, DEAland.
See
 Is The War On Cannabis A Cult? Taking Cannabiphobia To New Depths Of Absurdity. A Method to Their Madness?

Is that what Canada wants to become? I don't think so.

Also please see MarijuanaNews Still Needs Your Help. An Appeal From Richard Cowan.
